dct_description_sm: This GitHub repository holds the code needed to analyze your tracking results in the Visualize folder. It also holds the WristVizualizer (Brown University) software installation package needed to view the animations you will compute.

This tutorial guides users through the process of loading and tracking bones, saving and verifying tracking results using Autoscoper, and animating/visualizing tracked bones with MATLAB. It provides step-by-step instructions for tracking foot, knee, and shoulder datasets, including required file paths, software installation steps, and troubleshooting tips.

The deposited data includes BVR images, partial volumes, and surface files from CT scans, calibration files, filter settings, bone transforms, reference tracking files, and configuration files for each trial. It also contains a ReadMe with information about this data, a folder structure to follow, and tutorial instructions.

The GitHub repository listed under Related Material provides all required MATLAB scripts, WristVisualizer (Brown University) download files, and tutorial documentation. By cloning the repository, the folder structure is automatically set up, requiring only the transfer of Dataverse data into the designated folders.

Note: When citing this dataset, please cite the JOVE paper listed under related citations as well.
dct_title_s: Autoscoper Tutorial for Foot, Knee, and Shoulder Tracking
